newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV FALLS AFTER POLL, SEEKING CLUES.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV FALLS AFTER POLL, SEEKING CLUES.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev opened at 1,600-1,630 per dollar, down from 1,535-1,545 on Friday due to higher dollar demand as the interbank market awaited for more clues after Saturday's general poll, dealers said.
A cut in the main interest rate and pending lifting of price controls also led to increased foreign currency demand.
"The lev lost some 60-80 (levs per dollar) due to short-covering ahead of formation of a new parliament and a new government. Dollar supply is low," one dealer said.
Foreign currency demand from large end clients like fuel and energy importers also pushed the lev down.
The electoral commision said on Sunday the Union of the Democratic Forces had won 52 percent of the votes cast, which would give them 136-137 seats in the 240-member parliament.
"The new government is very likely to follow the economic policies of the interim one but it is advisable to be more cautious until we see it in office," another dealer said.
The interim government was expected to lift price controls on Monday as part of structural reform package agreed with international lenders.
"Uncertainty whether prices will rise sharply once controls are lifted makes clients reluctant to sell dollars," traders said.
A cut in the central bank main interest rate to 8.03 percent monthly, which went in force today also made investors cautious, traders said.

Domestic and foreign investors have pared foreign exchange positions in favour of high yield lev-denominated instruments in March and the first half of April as the main interest rate stood between 18 percent and 14.15 percent. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
